query_text: Why does my cat kick its toys when playing with them?

message.content:
Your cat kicks its toys due to deeply rooted natural instincts. This behavior, commonly known as the "bunny kick," serves multiple purposes:

## Hunting Instinct

Even well-fed domestic cats retain strong predatory instincts from their wild ancestors. When your cat grabs a toy with its front paws and rapidly kicks with its hind legs, it's mimicking the **killing bite** or **prey subduing** technique used in the wild. In a real hunt, cats use this maneuver to hold prey with their front paws while delivering powerful kicks with their back legs to disorient or disable it. This is essentially the "finishing move" of the hunting sequence.

## Play and Practice

Kittens learn bunny kicking during early play sessions with their mothers and littermates. These mock fights are crucial training grounds where they develop coordination, strength, and hunting skills. Adult cats continue this behavior with toys to keep their skills sharp and satisfy their primal urges in a safe way.

## Self-Defense

The bunny kick also serves as a defensive maneuver. If a cat finds itself on its back during a confrontation, its belly becomes exposed—a vulnerable position. Those powerful hind legs can kick away a threat, protecting vital organs and creating an opportunity to escape.

## Physical and Mental Benefits

This kicking behavior provides excellent **full-body exercise**, engaging core muscles, hind leg strength, and cardiovascular health. It also offers mental stimulation and stress relief, as performing natural hunting behaviors releases endorphins and reduces anxiety.

## When to Be Cautious

While normal with toys, bunny kicking directed at you or other pets can signal **overstimulation**—your cat's way of saying "this is getting too intense." Watch for warning signs like flattened ears, hissing, piloerection (hair standing up), stiff posture, or rapidly swishing tails.

Providing appropriate kicker toys gives your cat a healthy outlet for this instinctive behavior while protecting your hands and arms!
